Good writing is clear writing. Short sentences help readers follow an idea from start to finish. Long sentences with many clauses, however, can hide the point and tire the reader before they reach the end of the thought.

When you edit, look for words you repeat and phrases that add little. Replace complicated words with simple ones where you can. Read the text aloud, because your ear will catch problems that your eye misses.

A good draft is not perfect on the first try. It improves with each careful pass, and the readability scores here show whether your changes are making the text easier to read.
